answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut is only met by moving volume to the low-cost quote, and the incumbent has already refused to reopen price, so negotiate_terms is blocked. Deferral is unsafe: the primary contract hard-expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, unlike the non-critical month-to-month case. Adding a second source is a second decision we do not have and would not replace expiring primary volume. Switching primary in 14 days onto a line at 94% with zero buffer would raise delivery risk; a stoppage would dominate TCO. memory_c1 is the directly applicable record: incumbent renewal kept integration and deliveries intact. memory_c2 (prior quick onboarding) is the main counter-argument and is the one record worth re-checking, but even if last year’s switch went smoothly it does not erase today’s no-buffer cutover risk. Renew the incumbent for continuity this cycle; revisit cost after the cliff.
